title: Integer division and remainder
goal: Compute the number of full groups and leftover elements after checking the divisor.

prerequisites.text: Know int and the two kinds of division.

terms.title: Quotient
terms.definition: Here the number of complete groups from / with a nonnegative integer dividend and a positive integer divisor.

terms.title: Remainder
terms.definition: The result of %. For a nonnegative dividend and a positive divisor, it is smaller than the divisor.

terms.title: Divisor
terms.definition: The right operand to / or %. Integer division and remainder require a nonzero divisor.

sections.title: How many groups fit
paragraphs: A workshop has 95 labels. Each full roll holds 24. To plan the work, find the number of full rolls and the number of loose labels.
With a positive divisor and a nonnegative dividend, a / b gives the number of complete groups and a % b gives the leftover count. The order matters: divide the item count by the group capacity.
Some input errors can be spotted before any calculations. In the example, read_numbers already checks the numbers and their ranges. This lesson focuses on the calculation after validation.

sections.title: Rolls of labels
paragraphs: The input is 95 24. Work out how many groups fit into 95 before reading the code and output.
Contract for the example: the first line is at most 79 bytes and contains two whitespace-separated integers with ranges 0–1000 and 1–1000. The program prints invalid if this contract is broken.
steps: The helper reads 95 and 24 from the first line. The condition accepts these values.
95 % 24 gives 23. The program prints the two numbers in order: 3 23.

sections.title: What to check before dividing
paragraphs: With a zero divisor, / and % on int have undefined behavior. The check for values[1] == 0 runs before either calculation.
This exercise rejects negative input. In general, C integer division truncates toward zero: -7 / 3 is -2 and -7 % 3 is -1.

sections.title: Check the remainder
paragraphs: Check the identity a == (a / b) * b + a % b for valid inputs. In the example 3 * 24 + 23 reconstructs 95.
When a is smaller than b, the quotient is 0 and the remainder is a. When the division is exact, its remainder is 0. Run those cases independently.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Check the exact quotient and remainder rules and how text is converted to long.

selfcheck.prompt: What does the program print for 95 24?
feedback: A fourth group needs one more label.
The remainder is smaller than 24 for this input.

selfcheck.prompt: What should the program do before computing anything for input 20 0?
feedback: Remainder with a zero divisor is also undefined.
0 20 is expected for a positive divisor greater than 20.

selfcheck.prompt: If a = 32 and b = 60, what are the quotient and remainder and how can you reconstruct the input from them?
selfcheck.feedback: There are 0 complete groups and 32 left over. Check with 0 * 60 + 32 = 32.

practice.title: Pulse queue
practice.task: A controller handles a fixed number of pulses per cycle. The first line of input (at most 79 bytes) gives a pulse count from 0 to 1000 and pulses per cycle from 1 to 1000. Print the number of complete cycles and pending pulses separated by a space. Keep the provided invalid output for a malformed first line.
criteria: For 60 60 the remainder is 0, and for 0 60 both results are 0.
Validation and the zero-divisor check remain before the calculations.
practice.hint: Keep the helper and check. Change only the two calculations after pulses and per_cycle are read.

steps.action: Write the expressions for cycles and pending.
steps.why: Each result needs a different operation.
steps.expected: Use / for complete cycles and % for pending pulses.

steps.why: An exact cycle, a queue smaller than a cycle, and a zero cycle size test different behaviors.
steps.expected: Observed stdout matches the expected text.

steps.action: Add your own case with a nonzero remainder.
steps.why: Reconstruct the input to verify the partition.
steps.expected: Complete cycles times cycle size plus pending pulses gives the original count.

exercises.title: Transfer the idea
exercises.task: Find the smallest positive pulse count for a cycle size of 7 which gives both a nonzero cycle count and a nonzero remainder. Run and explain it.
criteria: Input 7 7 still gives a zero remainder.
